_comment: Invented notes and questions for testing search changes on a dev database. Nothing here is real. Notes are captured in order, so later notes are newer. Each question names the note (by key) that should come back.

notes.t: Ordered the Emlid RS3 RTK base station from the survey supplier today. Expected delivery in two weeks. Cost was 2,800 dollars.
Got a quote from Halvorsen Fencing for the back pasture: 4,200 dollars for 300 feet of woven wire. Marta said to wait until spring.
The well pump pressure switch is cycling too often. Cut-in is 40 psi, cut-out 60. Tank precharge should be 38 psi; it measured 22. Need to add air.
Changed the oil in the F-250 at 148,300 miles. Used 15 quarts of 15W-40 and a Motorcraft FL-2051S filter.
Dana's birthday is March 14. She mentioned wanting a pottery wheel but has no space for one until the garage is cleared.
Plan for the garage: sell the old table saw, move the bikes to the shed, and build shelving on the north wall. Target is to finish before March.
The Mavic 3 Enterprise batteries are at 180 cycles each. DJI rates them for 200. Budget for a new set of three before the summer mapping season.
Call with Rob Henley about mapping his 80 acre orchard. He wants orthomosaic plus a tree count. Quoted 1,900 dollars. He will decide after harvest.
Idea: put all the cameras on their own VLAN with no internet access, and let only the NVR reach them. Would need a firewall rule for the doorbell.
Switched the hens to the 18 percent layer pellet from the co-op. Egg count went from 9 a day to 12 within two weeks.
Dentist appointment for Leo moved to the 22nd at 3:30 pm. Dr. Okafor's office wants the insurance card again.
Sourdough notes: 78 percent hydration works best with the local flour. Bulk ferment 5 hours at 76 degrees. The 82 percent attempt was too slack to shape.
The tractor PTO clutch slips under load with the brush hog. Dealer says the clutch pack is about 1,400 dollars installed. Could adjust it first.
Drone liability insurance renews in August. Current policy is 1 million through SkyWatch at 62 dollars a month. Ask about a hull coverage add-on.
Leo's teacher Ms. Brandt says he is ahead in math and should try the after-school robotics club on Thursdays.
Solar quote from Ridgeview Energy: 9.6 kW array, 24 panels, 27,500 dollars before the tax credit. Payback estimated at 9 years.
Tomatoes: the Sungold and Cherokee Purple did best. Blight hit the Brandywines in August. Next year plant them in the east bed with more spacing.
Marta recommended the book The Overstory. Also wants to read something about beekeeping before deciding on hives.
The Zigbee network drops the barn sensors when the microwave runs. Moved the coordinator to channel 25 and added a repeater plug in the mudroom.
Business mileage so far this year: 4,120 miles for mapping jobs. Keep logging in the notebook in the truck door.
The Emlid RS3 RTK base station arrived this morning, a week early. Firmware updated and it gets a fix in under a minute on the tripod by the barn.
Decided against the Halvorsen woven wire quote. Going with high-tensile electric instead, doing the labor ourselves. Materials about 1,100 dollars.
Added air to the well pressure tank, precharge now 38 psi. Pump runs about 90 seconds per cycle instead of 20. Problem solved.
Rob Henley confirmed the orchard job. Flying the week of the 20th if the weather holds. He added a second block, so the price is now 2,400 dollars.
Bought three new Mavic 3 Enterprise batteries. The old set is retired to bench testing only. Serial numbers logged in the equipment sheet.
Got Dana a gift certificate for a six-week pottery class at the arts center instead of a wheel. Class starts in April.
New tires on the F-250: Toyo Open Country AT3, load range E. Paid 1,380 dollars installed at 151,000 miles.
Met Sam Ortiz at the county extension office. He runs the soil lab and offered a discount on bulk sample testing for mapping clients.
Dropped off 12 soil samples from the Henley orchard with Sam Ortiz. Results in about ten days. He wants the sample GPS points as a CSV.
Camera VLAN is live. Cameras are on VLAN 40 with internet blocked. The doorbell needed an exception to reach its cloud relay or notifications stopped.
Marta decided on two beehives for next spring. Ordered Langstroth kits and a nuc reservation from the apiary in the next county.
Decided to hold off on the Ridgeview solar array for a year. Roof needs replacing first, quote for that is 14,000 dollars.
Leo joined the robotics club. First competition is in February. He needs a laptop that can run the programming software.
Generator maintenance: ran it under load for 30 minutes, changed the spark plug, stabilizer added to the fuel. Next service in six months.
Chili recipe that everyone liked: two pounds chuck, three dried anchos, one chipotle, a tablespoon of cocoa, simmer three hours. No beans for Dana.
Adjusted the tractor PTO clutch per the manual, three flats on each bolt. No more slipping with the brush hog. Did not need the dealer.
New pricing for mapping jobs: 20 dollars an acre for orthomosaic, minimum 600 dollars, tree counts add 4 dollars an acre.
Passports for the whole family expire next year. Leo's expires first, in May. Renewal by mail takes about eight weeks.
Bought 120 bales of second-cut grass hay from the Lindqvist farm at 7 dollars a bale. Stacked in the east bay of the barn.
Set up the RTK base to broadcast corrections over NTRIP through the Emlid caster. The rover in the truck picks it up within 10 kilometers.
